violated_contract: A content decision that every processed record must pass (keep versus discard) cannot be skipped as a side effect of an unrelated caller flag. `process_conversation(force_process=True)` meant both "run enrichment now, do not defer" and "skip the discard gate", and four of six production callers pass it on a conversation's FIRST processing: the offline-sync append, POST /v1/conversations, POST /v1/conversations/{id}/finalize, and desktop first-open enrichment. Nothing fails: the flag was documented as a reprocess switch, each caller's tests stay green, and the skipped gate leaves no trace. Measured on a real account 2026-09-23, 12 of 13 junk conversations in two days ("Brief Acknowledgment", a 0.32 s "Oh") came from the sync path with full LLM summaries, and the read-side fragment filter then treated those generated summaries as evidence the user cared.
canonical_prevention: Callers state why they process (`ProcessingTrigger`), and one policy table (`backend/utils/conversations/relevance.py::RELEVANCE_POLICY`) decides whether that trigger assesses relevance; only user actions (first open, reprocess, merge) keep without assessment. The decision is one tiered function (user restore, stdlib-only rules, then the model) whose outcome is stored on the conversation and counted by trigger and deciding tier, so a path that skips the gate shows up in `conversation_relevance_decision_total{decided_by="policy"}` instead of in a user's list. Visibility protection comes only from user actions, never from generated output.
